decisions.title: Too busy to be tired
decisions.situation: Hugo says it is time for a nap. You have been awake for ages and have only inspected half the room.

choices.label: Give your eyes a short test closure
Ask Hugo to stay for a minute
Explain your position at full volume

result.title: Test extended
result.body: You wake up later. The uninspected half of the room is still there.

journal.text: I fell asleep while checking whether I needed a nap.

decisions.title: A very small food critic
decisions.situation: Hugo puts a birthday cake in front of you. Everyone waits for a photograph. You have a different artistic vision.

choices.label: Apply cake directly to face
Offer Hugo a sticky handful
Inspect this suspicious new object

result.title: The photograph survives
result.body: The cake does not. Hugo laughs so hard the first photo is mostly ceiling.

journal.text: I wore my birthday cake. Hugo kept the photograph.

decisions.title: Two is more than one
decisions.situation: Your biscuit breaks in half. There are now two biscuits, although something about the total feels suspicious.

choices.label: Fit the halves back together
Celebrate the extra biscuit
Count all the little crumbs

result.title: The original arrangement
result.body: The edges match. You test them twice before accepting that both pieces were one biscuit.

journal.text: I fitted two broken biscuit halves back together.

decisions.title: Launch delayed
decisions.situation: You turn a cardboard box into a rocket. Hugo says dinner is ready. Mission Control has terrible timing.

choices.label: Invite Hugo aboard
Finish one last countdown
Refuse to return to Earth

result.title: Crew shortage solved
result.body: Hugo puts one foot in the box. The rocket is now full.

journal.text: My cardboard rocket carried me and one of Hugo’s feet.

decisions.title: A very close race
decisions.situation: Your shadow keeps reaching the wall before you. You try standing still. It has apparently thought of that too.

choices.label: Make it do a silly dance
Move closer to the light
Sit down beside it

result.title: An obedient rival
result.body: You stop trying to beat the shadow and give it increasingly ridiculous instructions.

journal.text: I made my shadow do a silly dance.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: Hostile snack takeover
decisions.situation: Leo offers a plain cracker for your favourite snack. They call the cracker “rare”. There are twelve more in the packet.

choices.label: Demand two snacks for your one
Eat your snack during the sales pitch
Split yours and spare the cracker

result.title: The negotiator gets greedy
result.body: Leo nearly agrees, then notices you smiling. They withdraw the cracker and their goodwill.

journal.text: I tried to turn Leo’s snack offer into a better deal for myself.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Hugo plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of
Trade one song each
Give a brutally concise review

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Hugo.

journal.text: I listened to Hugo’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Hugo one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Stop before they can demonstrate
Agree on one round each, then stop
Demand rematches until you win

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Hugo seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Hugo I would.

decisions.title: Your stand-in has a meeting
decisions.situation: To dodge chores, you left a dummy in your dressing gown at your desk. Hugo is now giving it a serious talk about responsibility. The dummy is handling it well.

choices.label: Step out and take over the discussion
Leave a second dummy to play Hugo
Stay hidden and let the dummy handle it

result.title: A noticeable improvement in posture
result.body: Hugo says the dummy already agreed to take the rubbish out. You do it while the dummy remains at the desk, apparently thinking about its future.

journal.text: I replaced a dummy during Hugo’s lecture and did the chore it had agreed to.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Hugo finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Watch it together
Ask to keep the recording private
Defend the bath theory

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Hugo remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Hugo.

decisions.title: Your signature has improved
decisions.situation: Hugo thanks you for volunteering to clean the classroom. The roster has your name in Leo’s handwriting. Leo suddenly becomes interested in the ceiling.

choices.label: Make Leo split the work
Show Hugo the handwriting
Walk out and leave Leo with it

result.title: A reluctant double act
result.body: Leo admits the trick and apologises while stacking chairs. You finish together; Hugo is glad the room gets done.

journal.text: I made Leo share a cleanup they had volunteered me for.

decisions.title: You are in verse two
decisions.situation: Leo asks you to help rehearse a song about everyone who has annoyed them. Your name appears in verse two. The rhyme is frankly weak.

choices.label: Suggest a better rhyme for your insult
Ask why you made the track list
Walk out before verse three

result.title: An unwilling co-writer
result.body: You improve the line and rehearse the chorus. Leo laughs, then admits that your original offence was borrowing a pencil.

journal.text: I helped Leo rehearse a song that included an insult about me.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about
decisions.situation: At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about
Claim you invented motivational seminars

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Take a moment before answering
Say you need a short break
Deliver the sharp reply

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

choices.label: Look around for a minute
Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: Evidence from a previous haircut
decisions.situation: Hugo sends you an old photograph. The haircut is difficult to defend. The memory attached to it is much better.

choices.label: Ask for the whole story
Save a copy and label it
Focus entirely on the haircut

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Hugo remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Hugo also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Barcelona unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Barcelona.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

decisions.title: A reminder that needs reminding
decisions.situation: You find a note you wrote to help remember something important. It says only, “The usual one, but different.”

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
Work backwards from the context
Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

result.title: A successful cancellation

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

Pass the microphone down the row

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.situation: At a free games afternoon, the caller bans shouting “Bingo!” until every number has been checked. A player beside you whispers that this is how dictatorships begin.

choices.label: Check your numbers and play along
Ask the rebel about their resistance plans
Shout “Bingo!” with an empty card

result.title: Order survives another round
result.body: You finish a peaceful game while the rebellion beside you struggles to remember whether they heard forty-six.
